title: Westbrook Retires: Payton, SGA Salute Ex-Sonics Pick
htmlContent:
Only a handful of people know what it means to carry an NBA franchise. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has learned that firsthand. His rise from a promising young guard into a two-time MVP and NBA champion has pushed the Oklahoma City Thunder into conversations about a potential dynasty.

One of the few people who truly understands that weight isRussell Westbrook.

The Original Face of the Thunder

Before Gilgeous-Alexander, there was Westbrook. The relentless guard helped define the NBA in the 2010s and was the heartbeat of Oklahoma City for more than a decade. He spent his first 11 seasons with the Thunder, and those years were the best of his career, including his 2016–17 MVP campaign, when he became the first player since Oscar Robertson to average a triple-double over a full season.

After Westbrook announced his retirement this past August, Gilgeous-Alexander was among those congratulating the future Hall of Famer on a legendary career. The Thunder are already working on ways to honor him, and a No. 0 jersey retirement feels like a matter of when, not if.

Two Stars, One Franchise, Separate Paths

The two never shared a locker room. In July 2019, each was part of a separate trade that reshaped the franchise. Gilgeous-Alexander arrived from the LA Clippers in the Paul George deal, while Westbrook was sent to the Houston Rockets in exchange for Chris Paul and draft compensation. Still, they are forever linked by their place in Thunder history. Most consider them the two greatest players ever to wear blue and orange.

Their connection started away from the court.

"We started off with the same agents, so that's where the relationship first built. He's honestly just a great human being. Despite what people have said about him in the past and stuff like that. Russ is amazing. He's always been a phone call away if I need something." — Shai Gilgeous-Alexander

A Relationship Built on Respect

Westbrook being there for Gilgeous-Alexander reads like something Thunder fans would dream up. It is hard to script a better story than the franchise's first homegrown superstar serving as a resource for the player who would eventually carry the team to a championship.

Many view the relationship as a true passing of the torch. Gilgeous-Alexander may now sit above Westbrook in the franchise's all-time rankings, but that takes nothing away from what Westbrook built. He was Oklahoma City's first beloved NBA superstar, the player who helped turn a relocated team into a Western Conference fixture.

"He's an A-plus human, an A-plus basketball player. It doesn't get better than Russ. He's my guy. Had a great career. Sad to see him go, though." — Shai Gilgeous-Alexander

A Young Franchise With a Deep List of Stars

If you count their starting point as the 2008 relocation from Seattle, the Thunder are the youngest franchise in the NBA. Even so, an impressive group of stars has spent part of their primes in Oklahoma City: Gilgeous-Alexander, Westbrook, Kevin Durant, Chris Paul, Paul George and more.

Seeing the top two names on that list form a genuine friendship is the kind of generational continuity every pro sports organization hopes for. Franchises spend years trying to build a culture that connects one era to the next. In Oklahoma City, that bridge formed naturally between two players who never even played together.

Gary Payton: "He's a Hall of Famer"

Westbrook's story also has roots in the Pacific Northwest. The Seattle SuperSonics selected him with the fourth overall pick in the 2008 NBA Draft, making him one of the last players the franchise drafted before relocating to Oklahoma City that summer.

Hall of Famer and SuperSonics legend Gary Payton recently reflected on Westbrook's career in an interview with LandonBuford.com.

"[It's] been a great career for him. He's a Hall of Famer. He's gonna be [great at] whatever he does after basketball. And I'm just hoping that he can come back and be a part of us sometime. … Even though he didn't play there, [it] should be good for [him] to come back and help us there." — Gary Payton

Payton's words carry weight in Seattle, where fans have long pushed for the NBA's return. Westbrooknever suited up for the Sonics in a regular-season game, but his name remains tied to the city's basketball history, and Payton clearly sees a place for him there.

A Legacy Secured

Westbrook leaves the game as one of the most ferocious competitors of his generation, the NBA's all-time leader in triple-doubles and the player who made Oklahoma City matter on the national stage. Gilgeous-Alexander has taken the franchise to heights it had never reached, but he is quick to credit the man who came before him.

For the Thunder, the bond between their two greatest players is more than a feel-good story. It is a reminder that the franchise's past and present are connected, and that the torch was handed off with respect.
excerpt: Russell Westbrook's retirement has drawn tributes from Thunder star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and SuperSonics legend Gary Payton, with both honoring the NBA's all-time triple-double leader as a Hall of Famer and a genuinely great human being.
